Il DXY è salito dello 0,21% a 98,30, mentre il TLT è salito dello 0,92% a 87,07. Il mercato sembra essere in attesa dei prossimi dati macroeconomici, come il PIL QoQ USA e il CPI Eurozona. sentiment.reason_en: The market sentiment is neutral today, with the S&P 500 up 1.20% and the VIX down 2.56% to 17.48. The DXY is up 0.21% to 98.30, while the TLT is up 0.92% to 87.07. The market seems to be waiting for upcoming macroeconomic data, such as the US GDP QoQ and the Eurozone CPI. Articles from BlackRock Investment Institute and Goldman Sachs Insights suggest a cautious view on the market, with a possible compression of rates.

Il mercato obbligazionario è in calo, con il TLT che sale dello 0,92% e il BTP 10Y che si attesta al 3,39%. Il mercato valutario è stabile, con l'EUR/USD che scende dello 0,24% a 1,17. Il prezzo del petrolio è in calo del 9,07% a $90,38. Gli articoli di BlackRock Investment Institute e Goldman Sachs Insights suggeriscono una view cauta sul mercato.
market_impact_summary.en: The stock market is up, with the S&P 500 gaining 1.20% and the STOXX 600 gaining 1.60%. The bond market is down, with the TLT up 0.92% and the BTP 10Y at 3.39%. The currency market is stable, with the EUR/USD down 0.24% to 1.17. The oil price is down 9.07% to $90.38. Articles from BlackRock Investment Institute and Goldman Sachs Insights suggest a cautious view on the market.

audio_script_it:
Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert.

Il Nikkei ha chiuso in rialzo dello 0.72%, Shanghai in calo dello 0.10%. Questo suggerisce un'apertura mista per i mercati europei.

Nella seduta di ieri, l'S&P 500 ha chiuso in rialzo dell'1.20%, il VIX è sceso del 2.56%. L'oro si mantiene sopra i 4850 dollari l'oncia, in rialzo dell'1.51%. Il petrolio è in calo del 9.07% a 90.38 dollari al barile. Il Dollar Index è salito dello 0.21% a 98.30.

Non ci sono eventi geopolitici significativi che potrebbero impattare sui mercati oggi.

Oggi si attendono dati macro importanti, ma non ci sono rilasci significativi previsti per oggi. Il PIL QoQ USA sarà rilasciato il 29 aprile. La BCE ha mantenuto i tassi di interesse invariati nella riunione del 2 aprile.

I flussi ETF mostrano un afflusso di 663.9 milioni di dollari.'}, {'altcoins': "Tra le altcoin, Ethereum scende dell'1.04% a 2294 dollari, Solana perde lo 0.16% a 84.70 dollari, mentre BNB guadagna lo 0.40% a 624.04 dollari."}, {'sentiment': 'Il Fear & Greed Index è a 29, in zona Fear.'}]

Grazie per aver ascoltato il nostro podcast finanziario. Per domani, tenete d'occhio l'andamento dei mercati europei e americani, e monitorate le notizie relative alle principali società quotate. Un saluto da Price Alert, arrivederci alla prossima puntata. Grazie per l'attenzione e a domani.
audio_script_en:
Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing.

Asian markets closed mixed. The Nikkei gained 0.72% to 58,899, while the Shanghai index edged down 0.10% to 4051.43. European and US markets are set to open cautiously.

In Western markets, the S&P 500 rose 1.20% to 7126.06, with the VIX dropping 2.56% to 17.48. The Dollar Index advanced 0.21% to 98.30. Gold holds above $4850/oz, up 1.51%. Oil prices plunged, with Brent crude down 9.07% to $90.38.

There are no major geopolitical events or macroeconomic data releases scheduled for today. The US GDP growth rate is due on April 29.

Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets. Bitcoin is down zero point six seven percent to seventy four thousand seven hundred forty four dollars. The ETF daily net inflow was six hundred sixty three point nine million dollars.

In altcoins, Ethereum is down one point zero four percent to two thousand two hundred ninety four dollars. Solana is down zero point one six percent to eighty four point seven dollars. Binance Coin is up zero point four zero percent to six hundred twenty four point zero four dollars.

The Fear and Greed Index is twenty nine, indicating a Fear classification.

Thanks for tuning in and we'll see you tomorrow. Have a great day and goodbye from Price Alert.

articles.title: Implementing the digital euro project
articles.snippet: The European Central Bank (ECB) is working on a digital version of the euro, a project started back in 2020 that is coming closer to fruition as the enabling EU legislation progresses. The ECB has designed a digital equivalent of cash, aimed at complementing physical euros for day-to-day payments. Its approach may be compared and contrasted with the US Federal Reserve’s reluctance to introduce a digital dollar and with the People’s Bank of China’s definition of the digital yuan largely as a bank deposit. articles.title: Book launch: World War Trade: Conflict, Containment, and the Emergent World Trading Order
articles.snippet: Globalization is not dying. It is being rebuilt. When the United States and China weaponized trade in 2025, many feared the collapse of the global economy. Markets plunged, supply chains fractured, and policymakers spoke openly of economic warfare. But the collapse never came. In his new book, World War Trade, published by the Centre for Economic Policy Research, Richard Baldwin argues that the real story is not the conflict between superpowers but how the rest of the world responded. Through quiet restraint, strategic adaptation, and a wave of new trade agreements, countries representing the…

articles.title: The F-35 Is a Masterpiece Built for the Wrong War
articles.snippet: Think of a violin made by a master craftsman: beautiful, precise, capable of extraordinary performance, but impossible to produce quickly or cheaply. It takes time, rare expertise, and materials that cannot be sourced at scale. You would not equip an entire orchestra with instruments like that. Yet that is essentially what the United States has attempted with its tactical air fleet.The F-35 program’s total lifetime cost is projected to exceed two trillion dollars, the most expensive Major Defense Acquisition Program in history. articles.title: Iran and the Indispensable Broker: How Pakistan Outmaneuvers India on the World Stage
articles.snippet: In Sept. 2025, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia signed a mutual defense pact, formalizing what decades of quiet cooperation had already made real. The defense pact signed in Riyadh was presented in official communiqués as a natural deepening of bilateral ties. It was that, but it was also something larger: The latest installment in a pattern that has persisted for half a century and that continues to confound the logic of power politics. articles.title: Germany Moves to Privatize Ex-Gazprom Unit SEFE
articles.snippet: The German government will begin the official process of privatizing the local unit of Russia’s Gazprom, which the previous government seized in 2022 after Russia invaded Ukraine and the EU imposed sanctions on Moscow. Dubbed SEFE, or Securing Energy for Europe, the state entity handles energy import and infrastructure operations. In light of that latter part, the German government plans to organize a capital-raising round for the company, aiming to secure between 1.5 billion and 2 billion euros, equal to some $1.76 billion-$2.35 billion.…

articles.title: U.S. Extends Sanction Waiver on Russian Oil for India
articles.snippet: Days after saying it would not extend a sanction waiver for Russian crude sold to Indian refiners, the U.S. Treasury Department changed its mind and extended the waiver for two weeks until mid-May. According to an Indian Express report, the U-turn appears to have come as a result of pressure exerted on Washington by importers that turned to Russian barrels to replace lost supply from the Middle East. articles.title: Bank bosses called to meeting with Reeves over impact of Iran war on UK economy
articles.snippet: HSBC, Barclays, Lloyds, NatWest and Santander will this week discuss with chancellor how to limit effects of conflict Middle East crisis – live updates The bosses of Britain’s “big five” retail banks have been summoned to a meeting with the chancellor, Rachel Reeves, this week to discuss how to limit the economic impact of the crisis in the Middle East triggered by the US and Israel’s attacks on Iran. The chief executives of HSBC, Barclays, Lloyds, NatWest and Santander have been asked to attend an emergency summit on Wednesday, amid increasing acceptance that a major economic hit from the Iran war is unavoidable. Continue reading...

articles.title: ‘I don’t want to waste the gas’: Uber and Lyft drivers reeling as fuel prices soar
articles.snippet: Drivers face dilemma of driving more or cutting back – and support from ride-share giants decried as ‘slap in the face’ Drivers for Uber and Lyft across the US are spending hundreds more dollars on fuel each month after the US-Israel war on Iran triggered a sharp rise in oil prices. Support offered by the ride-hailing companies amounts to a “slap in the face”, drivers operating their services told the Guardian, as many are forced to choose between driving more to make the same money as previously – or cutting back their miles to reduce costs. Continue reading...
